E-7 · 2026-07-18engine 2026-07-18-restoration-provision-remeasurement-rate-v1
Affected: restoration-provision-remeasurement-rate

The make-good (restoration or dismantling) provision is now re-measured at the correct discount rate when you change its estimate. When you record a restoration remeasurement (for example the estimated make-good cost changes from 30,000 to 45,000), a new optional field lets you enter the current market-based discount rate for that provision at the remeasurement date. Previously the calculator discounted the revised estimate at the lease's own discount rate, which is not what the standards require: a restoration obligation is a separate IAS 37 provision, and IFRIC 1 with IAS 37 paragraph 47 re-discount it at a current market-based rate at the date of the change, which can differ from the lease rate. On the standard example this moves the remeasured provision from 34,431.05 (discounted at the lease's 5.5%) to 33,626.62 (at a 6% current market rate). The whole change adjusts the right-of-use asset; a decrease that would take the asset below zero is floored at zero with the excess going to profit or loss. If you leave the new rate blank the calculator falls back to the current lease rate as a proxy and shows a clear note asking you to enter the actual current market rate, so a defaulted figure is never silent. Leases that do not carry a restoration remeasurement, or that leave the new rate blank, are unchanged to the cent from before.

REG-f (blind-export-review-0717, L2/L4 ruling REGF-RULING.md; grounded IFRIC 1 para 3(b)/4 + IAS 37.47, both fetched verbatim from ifrs.org primary 2026-07-18 - not in the IFRS-16-only RAG, so cited by located primary text, not a RAG hit). ROOT: a restoration/dismantling obligation is an IAS 37 provision and a component of ROU cost (IFRS 16.24(d)/16.25), NOT part of the lease liability, so the IFRS 16 rate rules (16.42(b)/16.43 original rate, 16.45 revised rate) do not govern it. On a restoration remeasurement the engine discounted the revised amount at effectiveMonthlyRate = the operative LEASE rate at the event period (= the original commencement rate absent a prior rate-changing mod), producing restorationProvisionAfter = 34,431.0459 on the dl06 fixture (30,000 -> 45,000 effective 01.01.2028, remaining 60 months, lease 5.5%). IFRIC 1 3(b)/4 + IAS 37.47 require a CURRENT market-based pre-tax rate at the remeasurement date; at the fixture's 6% that is PV(45000,6%,60mo) = 33,626.6178 (annual-effective, engine convention; Delta 804.43, immaterial but a genuine non-conformance). FIX: a new PER-EVENT input restoration_discount_rate rides inside modificationEventsJson on restoration_remeasurement rows (raw-string pass-through, parsed ONLY by parsePercentInput - sidesteps the 1.452->1452 rate-parse class bug). When present the engine derives a provision monthly rate (1+annual)^(1/12)-1 and discounts the revised provision at it (server-action-calculate discountFactor + the provision unwind-rate switch from the event period onward), so the whole change adjusts the ROU cost (IFRIC 1.5(a)); a decrease floors the ROU at zero with the excess to P&L (IFRIC 1.5(b), the twin of IFRS 16.39, verified this turn: rouOpeningAfterModification = 0 when the decrease exceeds the ROU). FALLBACK (Adam product decision B): a blank rate defaults to the CURRENT lease rate as a disclosed proxy and raises a VISIBLE advisory on the calculator (the MODIFICATION_RESTORATION_REMEASUREMENT_APPLIED message), the export (event label + the PerMod 'Restoration provision remeasurement rate' detail row), and the manage-leases saved-lease card - never the stale original rate, never a silent wrong number (UI-blocking-principle / user-clarity law). NON-BREAKING BY CONSTRUCTION: off-by-default. A committed-engine differential (git HEAD vs working tree over restoration + consideration + scope-decrease + scope-increase scenarios) proved the ONLY change is the two new echo fields (restorationProvisionRatePercent, restorationProvisionRateDefaulted) plus the advisory message text, with ZERO numeric moves; the new echo fields are emitted restoration-ONLY (conditional spread) so every non-restoration modification result is byte-identical. GOLDEN IMPACT: exactly ONE golden fingerprint moved - mixed-chain-stress (it stages a restoration remeasurement, so its restoration event now carries the two new fields + the advisory) 28884ab580e2b632 -> da74085e370d84f7; the other six goldens are byte-identical (capture-mode confirmed all six equal their pinned values). The re-baseline is authorised by the INDEPENDENT committed-engine differential (zero numeric moves, det-law-2 - not capture-because-current), and the goldens were re-signed (registry P0 signature 49df939f). Cache version bumped so the saved-lease drift advisory reaches any user with a restoration remeasurement. SURFACE PARITY: tools/surface-parity-contract.js was extended with a MOD-EVENT SUB-FIELD sub-contract (previously blind to JSON-nested per-event keys) asserting each per-event field flows serializer -> engine raw-echo -> client input-state hydrate whitelist -> manage-leases display -> export; bite-proven both directions (dropping any leg goes RED). Regression oracle: tests/unit/restoration-provision-rate.test.js (11 tests): figure oracle 33,626.6178 to the cent, bite-proven RED against an in-memory mutant that reverts the discount to the lease rate; the entered rate drives it (5.5% reproduces the legacy 34,431.0459); save->hydrate round-trip survives the whitelist; the parity sub-contract holds and bites; off-by-default byte-identical control; the blank-rate advisory (visible, never stale-original); and the c137 class (increase / decrease / floor-to-zero IFRIC 1.5(b) / no-rate fallback). SCOPE NOTE: the INITIAL restoration provision's rate at commencement (also currently the lease rate) is a separate, larger change and is explicitly OUT of scope for this wave (Adam D0 is the remeasurement input only).

E-6 · 2026-07-18engine 2026-07-18-exempt-ignored-idc-class-close-v1
Affected: exempt-lease-with-ignored-figure-event

Completes the previous change (E-5) by closing the whole class: on a short-term or low-value exempt lease, initial direct costs are no longer left out in silence either. The exemption straight-lines only the lease payments, so a cost of obtaining the lease (initial direct costs) is not folded into the expense; but previously it also raised no note, so a workbook carrying a material set-up cost could still certify as ready. It now raises the same action-required note already raised for a residual value guarantee, a termination penalty or a purchase-option price, and the workbook can no longer certify ready until you resolve it. No figure a user could have seen changes — the straight-line expense is unchanged; only the note and the workbook readiness status change.

DEF-1 CLASS COMPLETENESS (diverse-lens follow-up, 2026-07-18). E-5 flagged the two events a blind reviewer happened to hit (termination penalty 16.27(e), reasonably-certain purchase-option price 16.27(d)). The defect CLASS is broader: ANY figure-bearing input silently dropped on an exempt lease. A full enumeration of every figure-bearing input the wrapper builds for an exempt lease (server-action-calculate params ~L11340-11369), run in isolation through the real calc action, found exactly ONE remaining silent drop: INITIAL DIRECT COSTS (16.24(c)). All other figure-bearing inputs already land in a faithful bucket: ABSORBED into the 16.6 straight-line expense (fixed escalation 16.27(a)/B42, rent-free, lease incentive — each a lease payment or a reduction of it), APPLIED as a clean term change / lease-term reassessment / reasonably-certain break (EXEMPTION_TERM_CHANGE_APPLIED re-spreads the SL over the revised term), FLAGGED at EXEMPTION_EVENTS_IGNORED@ACTION_REQUIRED (CPI/index, consideration/scope, RVG, termination penalty, low-value PO price, restoration — no on-point exempt convention), or BLOCKED (short-term + reasonably-certain PO is an Appendix A mutual-exclusion error). Variable/turnover rent (16.38) carries no amount input (a yes/no disclosure flag) so there is no figure to drop, and the discount rate is irrelevant on an SL-only exempt lease — both documented nothing-to-flag, not silent drops. IDC ROOT CAUSE: the exempt branch (runExemptLease) opts out of paragraphs 22-49, where the ROU-plus-IDC mechanics live (IDC is added to the ROU under 16.24(c) on full recognition), so a non-zero initialDirectCostsRaw had no home and was silently dropped — the SL total excluded it with issues=[] (reproduced: short-term 10x1,200 exempt lease + IDC 5,000 returned total 12,000, issues=[]; the full-recognition control lands the 5,000 in parsed.initialDirectCosts). FIX: exemptHasIdc (initialDirectCostsRaw parsed > 0) pushes the label "initial direct costs" into the same ignoredEventLabels set, raising EXEMPTION_EVENTS_IGNORED@ACTION_REQUIRED. IFRS grounding (search_ifrs16, VERIFIED 2026-07-18): 16.6 recognises only the LEASE PAYMENTS on a straight-line basis; lease payments are the App A / 16.27 components (fixed less incentives, index/rate variable, RVG, PO price, termination penalty) — IDC is NOT among them; it is a cost of obtaining the lease (16.24(c)), and C10(d) even treats it as a discrete, separately-excludable amount at transition. So IDC has no on-point exempt convention and the R26-consistent, non-inventing treatment is to FLAG it (auto-folding it into the SL would invent a convention 16.6 does not prescribe and silently move the total). NO COMPUTED FIGURE CHANGES: the amount is not folded into the SL (total stays 12,000); only the issues array and the downstream workbook technical-certificate status (READY -> ACTION_REQUIRED for an exempt lease carrying IDC) change. No golden scenario covers an exempt lease with IDC, so the golden set and sha are UNCHANGED (git diff docs/ai/golden-scenarios.json empty; pinned E-5 hash). userFacing because workbook readiness flips; cache bumped so the drift advisory reaches any affected user. Regression oracle: tests/unit/exempt-events.test.js was converted from the two DEF-1 point-tests to a TABLE-DRIVEN class test asserting the COMPLETE enumerated set (16 rows, each input -> its faithful bucket: ABSORBED total-moves / APPLIED re-spread / FLAGGED named-and-SL-unchanged / BLOCKED), plus a class-denominator check (every figure-bearing input has a row; a c109 negative control proves the matcher reports absence) and a two-marker mutation bite proof (reverting the termination-penalty OR the IDC label drops that flag; the shipped engine flags both). 33/33 GREEN.

E-5 · 2026-07-18engine 2026-07-18-exempt-ignored-termination-po-flag-v1
Affected: exempt-lease-with-ignored-figure-event

A short-term or low-value exempt lease that also carried a termination penalty, or a reasonably-certain purchase-option price, no longer leaves that amount out in silence. The exemption straight-lines the payments and has no liability to remeasure, so the calculator does not fold the end-of-term amount into the expense; but previously it also raised no note, so a workbook carrying a material penalty could still certify as ready. It now raises the same action-required note it already raised for a residual value guarantee, and the workbook can no longer certify ready until you resolve it. No figure a user could have seen changes — the straight-line expense is unchanged; only the note and the workbook readiness status change (they now correctly refuse to sign off over an unadjusted figure).

DEF-1 (diverse-lens blind round + L2 against the R26 floor, 2026-07-18). runExemptLease (server-action-calculate.full.bubble.txt) builds an ignoredEventLabels set that raises EXEMPTION_EVENTS_IGNORED at ACTION_REQUIRED severity for every figure-bearing subsequent event the 16.6 straight-line expense does not reflect (CPI/index, consideration/scope, residual value guarantee, restoration, and a term change tangled with a payment/CPI/scope change). Two event types were missing from that set: a termination penalty (16.27(e)) and a reasonably-certain purchase-option exercise price (16.27(d)). Reproduced: dl20 (short-term exempt + terminationPenaltyRaw 9,000) returned issues=[] with the 9,000 in zero figures (the workbook could certify READY over a material omission); a low-value exempt lease with a reasonably-certain PO exercise price 50,000 did the same. The RVG path (dl17) already flagged correctly, so the flag machinery existed and worked — the two event types were simply not enumerated. FIX: added exemptHasTermination (terminationPenalty parsed > 0, no reasonably-certain gate because the entered End Date already reflects exercising the termination option, mirroring the full-recognition path) which pushes the label "a termination penalty"; and for the purchase option, pushed the label "a purchase option exercise price" when the PO is reasonably certain AND the exemption is low-value (exemptionType !== short_term), because short_term + a reasonably-certain PO is ALREADY a BLOCKING mutual-exclusion error (EXEMPTION_SHORT_TERM_WITH_PURCHASE_OPTION, App A) and must not be double-signalled. IFRS grounding: 16.5-16.6 (the exemption opts a lease out of 22-49 and straight-lines the payments, so an end-of-term amount is not folded into the expense — get_ifrs16_paragraph verified 2026-07-18), 16.27(d)/(e) (both are figure-bearing lease-payment components), ruling R26 FLOOR (Amendment A: an exempt lease may carry no schedule, but an ignored figure-bearing event must be surfaced at ACTION_REQUIRED so the certification gate refuses READY, never silently dropped). NO COMPUTED FIGURE CHANGES: exempt leases carry no schedule and the amount is not folded into the straight-line expense (dl20 total stays 12,000 = 10 x 1,200; low-value PO stays 12,000); the only change is the issues array (a new ACTION_REQUIRED note) and the downstream workbook technical-certificate status (READY -> ACTION_REQUIRED for these two cases). No golden scenario covers an exempt lease with a termination penalty or PO, so the golden set and its sha are UNCHANGED (git diff docs/ai/golden-scenarios.json empty; changelog verifier goldens-sha gate satisfied by the pinned E-4 hash). This is nonetheless userFacing because the workbook readiness a user sees flips, so the cache version is bumped and the saved-lease drift advisory reaches any affected user. Regression oracle (finding-to-oracle, RED-pre / GREEN-post, bite-proven both directions in-process against a reverted engine that drops the label): tests/unit/exempt-events.test.js, new describe "DEF-1" (termination penalty flags ACTION_REQUIRED + names the penalty; SL unchanged at 12,000; workbook -> ACTION_REQUIRED; low-value PO flagged + named; NO DOUBLE-FLAG on short_term+PO which stays BLOCKING; c110 negative control a NON-exempt lease with a penalty raises no exempt flag).

E-4 · 2026-07-18engine 2026-07-18-terminal-liab-balloon-stub-horizon-v1
Affected: term-shortening-modification-with-end-of-term-balloon, multi-modification-scope-decrease-with-end-of-term-balloon

A correction to how an end-of-term amount (a residual value guarantee, a purchase-option exercise price or a termination penalty) is measured when a modification shortens the lease term. Previously, on certain term-shortening modifications the liability schedule finished with a small negative balance at the revised lease end (from a few cents up to about 2,450 currency units on the affected test cases) instead of unwinding exactly to zero, because the end-of-term amount was discounted over a slightly longer horizon than the schedule actually ran. The end-of-term amount is now discounted over exactly the same remaining time the schedule uses, so the liability unwinds to zero at the revised lease end by construction. Only leases that combine an end-of-term amount with a term-shortening modification (or a modification stack that reduces the scope) are affected; all other leases are unchanged to the cent.

ROOT CAUSE (server-action-calculate.full.bubble.txt, applySupportedModificationPackage balloon carry): the modification-path balloon PV was discounted over the INTEGER period count (revisedMonthlyPeriods.length - (effectivePeriodIndex - 1)), while buildScheduleWithOpeningOverrides accretes the liability over the SUM OF MONTH-FRACTIONS (calculateDiscountPeriodsToPayment). When rebuildMonthlyPeriodsPreservingHistory splits a term-shortened lease’s trailing day into a partial stub period (monthFraction < 1, e.g. 1/31), the integer count overstated the discount horizon, the balloon PV came in too small, and the full-nominal booking at the final period left a NEGATIVE terminal residue (the register’s TERMINAL_LIAB class: 19 export-focus combos, residues -6.92 to -2,451.96). FIX: the balloon now discounts over calculateDiscountPeriodsToPayment(revisedMonthlyPeriods, "In arrears", effectivePeriodIndex-1, last) — the identical fraction-sum horizon the schedule accretes — and the modification-trace pv_table row carries the same corrected discount_factor, so the trace still foots to the schedule opening (WBGATE-F2 preserved). The balloon settles at the final period’s END after that period’s full interest in BOTH timings, hence the inclusive (in-arrears) horizon. Byte-identical whenever every remaining period is a full month (fraction sum == integer count): the base path, CPI path, reassessment path and clean-boundary modifications are unchanged (verified empirically — reassessment extension to a mid-month end and a base lease with a partial final month both footed to zero before and after). IFRS grounding: 16.27(c)/(d)/(e) (the balloon is part of the lease payments), 16.45 (revised-rate remeasurement of the revised payments), 16.46(a) (a term-shortening derecognition leaves the surviving liability to unwind to exactly zero at the revised end); ruling R24 (the balloon is carried forward in full — unchanged by this fix, which corrects only its discount horizon). ALSO IN THIS RELEASE (test-oracle only, no figure change): the export-focus comboExpectScopeDecreaseGuard secondary check was corrected to assert the R24 carry-forward (final payment = revised rent + full nominal) instead of the pre-R24 exclusion it still asserted — the 5 multiModStack-scopeDecrease register rows were this stale oracle, not an engine defect (the engine footed to zero and carried the balloon on all 5). Golden scenarios unchanged (no golden combines a balloon with a stub-bearing term-shortening modification); goldens sha unchanged. Regression oracle (finding-to-oracle, RED-pre/GREEN-post, bite-proven both directions in-process against a reverted integer-horizon engine mutant, +0.01 perturbation bites, c109/c110 controls): tests/unit/terminal-liability-unwind.test.js. Register entry TERMINAL_LIAB moved to resolved in docs/ai/known-defect-tests.json in the same commit.

E-3 · 2026-07-18engine 2026-07-18-exempt-events-rou-horizon-cpi-scopedec-v1
No user-visible figure changes

A maintenance re-baseline of the golden replay fingerprints, with no change to any figure. A recent release added a deterministic diagnostic field to every modification result, which moves the fingerprint that hashes the whole result while leaving every monetary value unchanged. Four modification-bearing golden scenarios had their recorded fingerprints refreshed to match. No figure a user could have seen has changed and no saved schedule is affected. This entry also corrects a note in the previous entry which said none of the affected classes were golden scenarios; that was not accurate for the fingerprint check.

The previous release (recorded as E-2, first committed as 255ed3ff) added a deterministic, input-derived boolean, meta.modificationRenegotiatedFlatPayment, to every modification result. It is read only inside the same-day index re-base gate and changes no figure on any lease without a same-day index event. The golden replay hashes the whole result object, so the mere presence of this new field moved the recorded fingerprint of four modification-bearing golden scenarios (published-mod-consideration, published-scope-decrease, scope-increase-inherits-cadence, mixed-chain-stress) while every monetary value, schedule row, right-of-use row, journal line and opening and closing balance stayed byte-identical to the pinned published benchmark. L2-GOLDEN adjudicated this with a biting differential that reported exactly one changed path and zero numeric moves per scenario, cross-checked against the independent pre-change engine (commit 255ed3ff caret) whose output reproduces the old pins exactly. The re-baseline was authorised only because each captured fingerprint equalled L2-GOLDEN's independently derived anchor (49a874da, ede55fd7, 6382671a, 28884ab5); it is not a capture-because-current. E-2's note that none of the three affected classes were golden scenarios was wrong for the fingerprint check: the E-B field surfaces in these four modification-bearing golden fingerprints even though no figure moved. The engine itself is unchanged, so the cache version is not bumped by this entry. The goldens were re-captured, re-signed, and the new content hash is pinned here.

E-2 · 2026-07-18engine 2026-07-18-exempt-events-rou-horizon-cpi-scopedec-v1
Affected: exempt-lease-subsequent-events, reassessment-and-term-shorten-ROU-depreciation-horizon, scope-decrease-same-day-CPI-rebase

Three corrections to how the calculator handles changes made after a lease has started. First, on a lease you have put on the short-term or low-value exemption, a later change is no longer left out in silence. If you extend or shorten the term, the straight-line expense is re-spread over the revised term. If you record a price-index change, a rent renegotiation, a residual value guarantee or a make-good provision on an exempt lease, the calculator now raises an action-required note explaining that the expense shown does not reflect that change, rather than quietly ignoring it, and a workbook with such a note can no longer certify as ready. A short-term lease whose revised term goes over twelve months, or that gains a purchase option, is flagged as no longer qualifying for the short-term exemption. Second, when a lease-term reassessment or a term-shortening change brings the lease end forward (for example a break option that becomes reasonably certain), the right-of-use asset now finishes depreciating at the revised lease end instead of carrying a value past the actual end of the lease. Third, the same-day index re-base that already applied to a rent renegotiation now also applies when the rent is renegotiated through a scope reduction, so recording a price-index reading on the day you reduce the scope no longer stacks that day's uplift on top of the newly agreed rent.

E-A (IFRS 16.5-16.7, 16.6; ruling R26 with Amendment A, L2 + L4 + cross-challenge; search_ifrs16 verified 2026-07-18: 16.5 opts a lease out of paragraphs 22-49, 16.6 straight-lines the payments over the lease term). An exempt lease has no liability, so the 16.40-46 remeasurement machinery does not apply and a subsequent event flows through the 16.6 straight-line expense. The exempt branch (runExemptLease) previously dropped CPI, modification, reassessment and residual-value-guarantee inputs with no warning, mis-stating the expense while still certifying READY. It now: (1) re-spreads the 16.6 expense over the revised term for a clean flat-rent term change (representative: r006 low-value, term extended 31.12.2033 -> 31.12.2036, expense 400,000 over 120 months -> 520,000 over 156 months at 3,333.33/month); (2) raises the existing EXEMPTION_SHORT_TERM_OVER_12_MONTHS BLOCKING exception when a term change takes a short-term lease over 12 months or adds a purchase option, re-tested at the change date (IFRS 16.7, supplied via L4 practice from ifrs.org 2025 primary text + BDO Australia; not returned by the paragraph RAG, so cited by provenance not as a RAG hit); (3) raises EXEMPTION_EVENTS_IGNORED at ACTION_REQUIRED severity for every other un-applied event (CPI, consideration or scope change, RVG, restoration, or a term change tangled with a payment/CPI/scope change), so the export certification gate refuses READY (Amendment A: a REVIEW-severity note would auto-resolve to Completed and let a mis-stated figure ship) and the message states the expense excludes the event. RVG timing and the low-value multi-year CPI re-spread have no published guidance (L4-verified), so the engine warns rather than inventing a convention. Workbook resolution verified: g04b (low-value + CPI) -> ACTION_REQUIRED, r006 (term applied) -> REVIEW_RECOMMENDED, clean exempt lease with no event -> READY_FOR_REPORTING and byte-identical (negative control). E-C (IFRS 16.32, search_ifrs16 verified 2026-07-18: 'Otherwise, the lessee shall depreciate the right-of-use asset from the commencement date to the earlier of the end of the useful life of the right-of-use asset or the end of the lease term'). When an applied lease-term reassessment or a term-shortening modification brings the lease end forward, the right-of-use asset now depreciates to the revised lease end. The useful-life decouple (depreciating past the lease end) is gated on a reasonably-certain purchase option, since only then does the lessee keep the asset; a non-purchase-option lease amortises to the earlier of useful life and the revised lease term. Representative: r005 (break option reasonably certain, RVG 47,000, no purchase option, break 31.12.2027) closing right-of-use asset at the break 26,471.39 -> 0.00, phantom depreciation to 31.12.2032 removed, revised remaining amount 30,442.10 re-spread over 9 months at 3,382.46/month. A purchase-option lease still depreciates past the lease end over the asset useful life (byte-identical control). E-B (IFRS 16.42, 16.45; extends BF-29). The same-day index re-base that suppressed a spurious CPI uplift on a same-day consideration change now also covers a scope-decrease that renegotiates the rent to an explicit flat amount. Representative: g05 (scope decrease to 15,833 with a same-day index 84) payment 13,299.72 -> 15,833.00, post-modification opening liability 68,272.04 -> 81,276.24, same-day CPI delta 0. Fenced: a scope decrease followed by a genuinely later CPI still reprices (15,833 -> 17,416.30 at index 110), and a consideration-change same-day CPI is byte-identical to BF-29. The suppression is NARROW (L2-blessed 2026-07-18, IFRS 16.42(b)/16.45(c)): it fires only when the entered rent is a GENUINELY NEW price level, different from both the inherited rent and the mechanically scope-scaled rent. A scope decrease whose entered rent merely CONTINUES the existing indexed stream still has its same-day index applied (a 30 percent scope decrease continuing a 25,000 rent with a same-day index 115 gives 25,000 x 0.7 x 1.15 = 20,125, not 17,500), because the index clause still determines those payments (16.42(b)); only a genuinely renegotiated flat rent is the revised contractual payment (16.45(c)) struck at the current price level and is not re-indexed on the same day. The round-1 same-day-CPI suppression for scope_decrease had been over-broad (it suppressed the continuing-stream case too, understating the obligation); this release narrows it. FROZEN-HISTORY NOTE: the E-C and E-B engine changes were committed on 2026-07-17 (commit 255ed3ff) without a cache-version bump or changelog entry, because their affected scenarios are not in the golden set so the goldens-hash gate did not require one; this entry records them together with E-A and bumps LEASE_ENGINE_CACHE_VERSION so the saved-lease drift advisory reaches any affected user. Golden scenarios unchanged; goldens sha unchanged. Regression oracles (RED-pre / GREEN-post, c109/c110 controls): tests/unit/rou-depreciation-horizon.test.js (E-C), tests/unit/cpi-anchor-rebase.test.js (E-B), tests/unit/exempt-events.test.js (E-A).

E-1 · 2026-07-17engine 2026-07-17-balloon-carry-cpi-rebase-v1
Affected: scope-decrease-with-RVG/PO-balloon, same-day-CPI-with-consideration-mod

Two corrections to how the calculator handles end-of-term amounts and same-day index changes when a lease is modified. First, when a modification reduces the lease scope, any end-of-term amount already in the liability (a residual value guarantee, a purchase-option price, or a termination penalty) is now carried forward in full into the reduced lease and settled at the end, instead of being dropped. Previously the schedule fell to zero at the change date with the guarantee never settled, which understated the liability. If your revised contract reduces the guarantee, you can now enter the revised amount expected to be payable and only the guarantee scales; the purchase-option price and any penalty are never scaled. Second, when you renegotiate the rent to a flat amount and record a consumer-price-index reading on the very same day, the calculator no longer applies that same-day index uplift on top of the newly agreed rent (which double-counted inflation the negotiated rent already reflected); the index anchor re-bases to that day's level, and any later index reading still applies normally. A separate warning was also added (no figures change) flagging the contradiction of a reasonably-certain purchase option held together with a residual value guarantee or a termination penalty.

BF-18 (IFRS 16.27(c)/(d)/(e), 16.42(a)/16.43, 16.45, 16.46(a); ruling R24, L2 money ruling + independent cross-challenge UPHELD): discrete end-of-term balloons carry forward unchanged through a scope-decrease / term-shorten derecognition; default full-persist, RVG scalable only via an explicit revised amount expected to be payable, PO price and penalty never scale. Representative difference (scenario x04, 40% scope decrease, RVG 40,000, revised rate 7.5%): post-modification opening liability 107,764.41 -> 139,962.83 (the 40,000 RVG PV of 32,198.42 was being dropped; understated by 19,319-32,198 depending on whether the guarantee scales). An active REVIEW_REQUIRED prompt is raised at the balloon-present + scope-decrease intersection. BF-29 (IFRS 16.42 anchor re-base): a same-day (at entry) consideration change re-bases the CPI index anchor to that day's level. Representative difference (scenario s23, renegotiate to 11,000 with a same-day index 105): post-modification liability 380,560.46 -> 362,438.53, payments 11,550 -> 11,000. Fenced: a modification followed by a LATER-day CPI (and a mid-month consideration change followed by a later-in-month CPI that only snaps into the same period) is byte-identical to before and reprices normally at the original commencement rate. BF-34/35 (IFRS 16.27(c)/(e)): non-figure-affecting WARN only (measurement unchanged this release; a full fix that excluded the RVG expected-payable and penalty when a purchase option is reasonably certain would move scenario s12 from 565,813.53 to 550,926.54). Baseline entry: the changelog system goes live. The engine reproduces the published worked examples catalogued on the proof page (from the IASB, the major accounting firms, specialist IFRS educators and other software providers), plus checkpoints derived independently from first principles, and passes the full governed suite. The proof page holds the live count and links to every example, so no other page repeats a number; the examples shown there are publicly deep-linkable and the rest run as test oracles only. No figure changes are recorded by this entry; it anchors the enforcement chain.

Figure-affecting changes are recorded here with the affected scenario classes, the size of representative differences, and the reason for the change.

Input-reading and display fixes that did not change the engine

10 entries
C-10 · 2026-07-18no engine change
Where: Calculator currency panel (IAS 21 FX Translation view); Schedule export FX Translation tab

The exchange difference on the lease liability translated the period's lease payment at the year's average rate. Where the period holds a single payment that settles on the reporting date, the average is not standing in for a spread of payments: the payment's own date is the reporting date, so its rate is the closing (spot) rate for that date (IAS 21.21, 21.8). Translating it at the average instead moved the shown exchange gain or loss by the payment times the gap between the average and closing rates. The view now translates a payment settling on the reporting date at the closing rate; where payments are spread across the period they keep the year average, which IAS 21.22 allows. The lease's own-currency schedule was never affected, the closing lease liability was always right, and the check that the exchange difference equals its independent build-up still ties.

Affected input shape: A foreign-currency lease shown in a presentation currency where a single lease payment falls on the reporting date and there is no other payment in the reporting period, such as a lease paying once a year in arrears looked at that year end. Window: From the currency features going live on 5 July 2026 until 18 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for saved schedules. The currency panel re-reads the saved rates and works the figure out again the next time the lease is opened. If you downloaded a schedule export with the FX Translation tab for a lease of this shape in the window above, generate it again.

C-9 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Schedule export Depreciation Walkthrough tab (leases whose end date was changed by a modification or reassessment)

Before the end-date change takes effect, the schedules correctly depreciate the right-of-use asset over the lease term that was in force at the time. The Depreciation Walkthrough sheet, which shows the working behind each period's depreciation, instead measured its 'Remaining Frame' on those earlier rows against the revised term. On a shortened lease that understated the frame, so Expected Depreciation ran too high and the Diff columns grew period by period; on an extended lease the frame picked up one month too many. Rows from the change date onwards were always right. As with the purchase-option correction (C-8), the actual depreciation in the ROU schedule, the journals and every balance were always correct; only the walkthrough's explanatory columns disagreed with them. The walkthrough now measures each row against the lease end in force for that row, and the workbook's walkthrough controls fail if the sheet ever disagrees with the schedule again.

Affected input shape: A lease with a modification or reassessment that changed the lease end date (shortened or extended), exported with the Depreciation Walkthrough sheet. The rows before the change date were affected. Window: From the walkthrough sheet going live on 12 June 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for the lease figures: the ROU schedule, journals and balances were always correct. If you exported a lease with an end-date change before 12 July 2026, ignore the Expected Depreciation and Diff columns on the rows before the change on that workbook's Depreciation Walkthrough sheet, or re-export to get a corrected sheet.

C-8 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Schedule export Depreciation Walkthrough tab (purchase-option leases)

On a purchase-option lease the schedules correctly depreciate the right-of-use asset over the asset's useful life rather than the lease term (IFRS 16.32). The Depreciation Walkthrough sheet, which shows the working behind each period's depreciation, wrongly measured its 'Remaining Frame' to the lease end instead of the useful-life end on the in-lease rows. So its Expected Depreciation, Depreciation Diff, Expected Closing ROU and Closing Diff columns were wrong on those rows: the Diff column grew from around one month's depreciation at the start to the entire remaining carrying amount at the final lease period, and Expected Closing ROU showed zero at lease end while the schedule correctly carried the asset into the owned-asset period. The actual depreciation numbers in the ROU schedule, the journals and every balance were always right; only the walkthrough's explanatory columns disagreed with them. The walkthrough now uses the same useful-life horizon as the schedules, and the workbook's walkthrough controls now fail if the walkthrough ever disagrees with the schedule again.

Affected input shape: A lease with a purchase option that is reasonably certain to be exercised and an asset useful life longer than the lease term, exported with the Depreciation Walkthrough sheet. Window: From the purchase-option features going live on 2 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for the lease figures: the ROU schedule, journals and balances were always correct. If you exported a purchase-option lease before 12 July 2026, ignore the Expected Depreciation and Diff columns on that workbook's Depreciation Walkthrough sheet, or re-export to get a corrected sheet.

C-7 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Calculator currency panel (IAS 21 FX Translation view); Schedule export FX Translation tab

For a lease that had been remeasured before the reporting date, the single-lease FX Translation view worked out the derived exchange difference by treating the whole remeasurement uplift as if it were translated at the closing rate. That overstated the exchange gain or loss and routed an amount that belongs to the right-of-use asset (IFRS 16.39) through profit or loss. Working out the exchange difference on a remeasured lease needs the rate on each event date, which this single-rate view does not hold, so it no longer shows a derived exchange difference for these leases: it shows the balances and points to the disclosure note, which translates the lease layer by layer at each event date. Leases with no remeasurement are unchanged, the lease's own-currency schedule was never affected, and the note figure was always right.

Affected input shape: A foreign-currency lease that had been remeasured (a CPI change, a modification or a reassessment) before the reporting date, viewed at a reporting date in the single-lease FX Translation view. Window: From the currency features going live on 5 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for saved schedules. If you read a derived exchange difference off the FX Translation view or the schedule export's FX Translation tab for a lease that had a CPI change, modification or reassessment before the reporting date, use the disclosure note's figure instead, which translates the lease correctly at each event date.

C-6 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Disclosure note (current and non-current lease liability split); Disclosure workbook

The current portion of the lease liability was worked out as the fall in the balance over the next twelve months. For a lease that is still accruing interest with no payment due in the coming year the balance rises, so this produced a negative current liability. The current portion is the part of the balance due within twelve months (IAS 1.69); when nothing is due in the coming year that part is nil, not a negative number, and the whole balance is non-current. The current portion is now held at nil for such a lease, which is the standard presentation. The total lease liability was always right.

Affected input shape: A lease whose liability grows over the next twelve months, such as a lease in a rent-free period with nothing paid in the coming year. Window: From the disclosure note going live on 5 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: None for saved schedules. If you downloaded a disclosure workbook showing a negative current lease liability in the window above, generate it again.

C-5 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Disclosure note (presentation-currency note); Disclosure workbook rates sheet

The average rate the note used to translate a year's interest was the average of the reporting month only. For a December year end that was the December average rather than the average across the whole year. Where rates moved through the year this put the interest line on the wrong average, with the difference absorbed into the exchange line, so the note still added up but the split between interest and exchange movement was off. The note now averages across the whole reporting year for the current year, and across the prior year for the comparative, which is the approximation IAS 21.40 intends. The total was always right.

Affected input shape: A foreign-currency lease shown in a presentation-currency note, where the average rate for the year was taken from the reporting month only. Window: From the disclosure note going live on 5 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: None for saved schedules. If you downloaded a disclosure workbook with a foreign-currency note in the window above, generate it again so the interest and exchange lines use the year's average.

C-4 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Calculator currency panel (IAS 21 view); Schedule export FX Translation tab

The exchange difference on these two views was worked out from the lease start to the reporting date and shown as a single entry to post. At a second or later year end that is the whole difference built up since the lease began, not the difference that arose in the year, so posting it every year would count earlier years again. The panel and the tab now show the exchange difference that arose in the period then ended (the twelve months to the reporting date), with the opening balance carried at the prior year end rate, which is what IAS 21.28 asks you to recognise. Interest for the period is translated at that year's average rather than an average running back to the lease start. Lease schedules in the lease's own currency were never affected, and the first reporting period is unchanged.

Affected input shape: A foreign-currency lease translated at a second or later reporting period, that is, a reporting date more than twelve months after the lease started. Window: From the currency features going live on 5 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for saved schedules. If you posted the exchange difference from one of these views at a second or later year end, compare it with the period movement shown now, and if you downloaded a schedule export with the FX Translation tab in the window above, generate it again. The currency panel now also asks for the rate at the prior year end so it can work out the movement for the year.

These boxes read European-style amounts with the separators swapped (5.000 was read as 5.00). Ledger amounts are typed fresh each time the note is built and are not stored, so no saved data was affected. The boxes now read amounts exactly like the calculator's own amount fields.

Affected input shape: Amounts typed with European separators (for example 5.000 meaning five thousand, or 1.234,56). Window: From the disclosure note going live on 5 July 2026 until 11 July 2026.

What to check: None. If you downloaded a disclosure workbook in the window above after typing a European-style ledger amount, generate it again.

C-2 · 2026-07-11no engine change
Where: Calculator CPI index input

A CPI index in the three-decimal shape was converted to a whole number before calculation (314.175 became 314175), overstating the index one thousand times. If a lease was calculated and saved with such an index, the saved schedule carries the converted number. The index is now passed to the engine exactly as typed, and an index containing a comma is stopped with a message asking for a dot decimal, because commas mean different things in different countries.

What to check: Open any saved lease that has CPI events and check the index box shows the number you meant. If it shows something like 314175 where you meant 314.175, correct it, recalculate and save again.
